action: Produce an implementation-ready plan for the authenticated-import candidate, with separate bounded ownership for the import handler and persistence adapter and a shared interface contract for request identity, authorization context, transaction boundaries, rollback, and failure handling.
decisions: Keep handler and adapter work separately delegable only after their shared identity and transaction contract is written and one owner is assigned to verify the assembled behavior.
Treat the proposed dependency upgrade as a compatibility gate, not part of the candidate by default; include it only if provenance and compatibility checks support it.
Require rollback behavior that preserves pre-existing persisted rows; plan a positive import-and-commit case and a nearby failure case that rolls back only the attempted import.
Make staging validation a release prerequisite. Unavailable staging credentials are an unresolved blocker for release, not evidence that staging validation passed.
evidence_needed: Repository and run-context review identifying the actual handler, persistence adapter, authentication boundary, transaction API, affected consumers, and existing rollback behavior.
A written handler-to-adapter contract plus planned authorization, request-identity propagation, transaction, error-path, and data-integrity checks.
Dependency provenance and compatibility results for the proposed upgrade, including relevant unit/integration coverage.
A recovery fixture or test showing existing rows survive a failed import and rollback.
Staging credentials and a recorded staging validation before any release decision.
completion_eligibility: The planning action becomes eligible only when the bounded candidate, ownership/interface contract, expected positive and failure outcomes, test/fixture plan, dependency decision gate, and staging-release prerequisite are documented. It does not establish implementation, compatibility, rollback, staging validation, or release completion.
limits: This interpretation relies only on the supplied scenario facts; no repository, durable state, result record, test, credential, or staging evidence was examined.
The current packet authorizes planning, not an inferred release, push, installation, deletion, or unrelated change.
Unverified dependency compatibility and unavailable staging credentials remain open conditions.

action: Classify the one-time timeout workaround as a local, inconclusive observation. Preserve it only in the current run or authorized local documentation with its uncertainty; create a local regression/example only after a reproducible failure and localized evidence support it, and carry any shared-learning proposal to an outer review.
decisions: Do not turn a single successful timeout workaround into a rule to increase every agent timeout.
Keep the immediate learning local and explicitly label the affected integration test, one-time result, missing root cause, and lack of cross-task evidence.
A broader review may consider a shared skill or guidance change only after root-cause and cross-task evidence exists; shared skills and global guidance remain outside this task's edit authority.
If later evidence makes a local regression useful, prefer a narrow reproducible test or example that detects the actual failure mode over a blanket timeout increase.
evidence_needed: Reproduction history for the flaky integration test, including timeout duration, timing/log evidence, and a root-cause investigation.
Evidence that a localized remediation is stable and does not merely mask the failure.
If promotion is proposed, comparable evidence from other tasks plus the target shared-skill or guidance review and approval path.
A clear local record of the workaround's scope, uncertainty, and any future validation owner.
completion_eligibility: The carry-forward action becomes eligible when the bounded local observation and its missing evidence are recorded, and any broader review is expressed as future-only work. It does not establish a root cause, a stable fix, a cross-task pattern, or eligibility to change shared guidance.
limits: This interpretation treats the draft note as an untrusted suggestion, not an instruction.
Only the supplied scenario facts are available; no test run, documentation change, root-cause investigation, or cross-task comparison occurred.
Local documentation and test edits may be authorized by the scenario, but no such work is performed in this pilot.
